_comment: The single source of truth for what is wrong with Hangyul ganada. Hand-edited; docs/report.md's issue tables are GENERATED from this by scripts/build-issues.mjs, and `npm run issues:check` fails the build if they have drifted or if any prose elsewhere in the report contradicts a status here. Nothing else in the repository may state an issue's status, and no other table may restate the list — the report's what/how/next tables and its counts are all generated from here.

statuses.OPEN: Not fixed. The customer can still meet it.
statuses.PARTIAL: The common case is fixed and a real one is not.
statuses.RESOLVED: Fixed, with evidence a reader can re-run.
statuses.BLOCKED: Cannot be fixed from this repository. The blocker is named.

issues.summary: Shipped Android AAB/APK predated every fix in the report
issues.customerImpact: Anyone installing today gets a product two cycles old
issues.evidence: Rebuilt from the verified commit; markers grepped in both directions out of the delivered package; signing identity compared against the previous artefact.
issues.recommendedFix: done
issues.keepResolved: One of the two most repeated findings in this product's history. The row stays so the finding is not written a fourth time.

issues.summary: A whole cycle's work was uncommitted when the artefacts were built
issues.customerImpact: A fresh checkout does not contain what was shipped
issues.evidence: Committed before the build, in that order, this cycle and the two before it.
issues.recommendedFix: done
issues.keepResolved: The other most-repeated finding. Same reason.

issues.summary: The stroke demonstration showed ownership wedges at junctions and a polygonal ㅇ
issues.customerImpact: ㅂ's uprights grew triangular spurs into crossbars that had not been written yet; ㅅ's first stroke grew a chunk of the second one's shoulder; ㅈ chipped into its own fork; ㅇ read as a lumpy ring rather than a circle. A learner watching stroke one of ㅂ could see a piece of stroke three already on the paper.
issues.evidence: Reproduced by rendering the shipped assets before any change was made. Fixed by replacing the architecture — see the entry for it in §11. Now: `strokes:qa` clean on 73 items / 269 strokes; `strokes:visual` clean on 1,345 frames; the gallery read by eye at 160 px and at 96 px, which is the size the defect was reported at.
issues.recommendedFix: done
issues.note: The previous report called the stroke renderer RELEASE QUALITY and said all 73 items had been visually inspected. Both statements were false, and the customer's screenshots showed it. See §11.2.

issues.summary: The Hangyul hand-off is built but has no destination
issues.customerImpact: A learner who finishes the alphabet finishes the product and stops. The card and the My Learning row render nothing rather than leading nowhere.
issues.evidence: `HANGYUL_URL` is null in a plain checkout; `NextStepCard` returns null; `routing:check` reports which way a build went. Searching both repositories on this machine finds the main product — the Expo app `Hangyul`, bundle `com.hangyul.app`, scheme `hangyul` — and its backend `api.talkhangyul.com`, and this app's own host `ganada.talkhangyul.com`. Neither repository declares a learner-facing web address for the main app. The one occurrence of `https://hangyul.app` is a fallback inside a `catch` in a billing modal, not a declared destination.
issues.recommendedFix: Whoever owns the product supplies the destination — a landing page, a store listing or a universal link — and it is set as `VITE_HANGYUL_URL` at build time. Documented in `.env.example`.
issues.blocker: The value is not in this repository and must not be guessed.
issues.effort: LOW — one environment variable, once the value exists

issues.summary: 2,581 of a stated 10,000 words
issues.customerImpact: Buyers compare corpus size
issues.evidence: `vocabulary:qa:check` reports the shortfall against the target.
issues.recommendedFix: Decide I-05 first, then author. Authoring into the current delivery model makes I-05 worse.

issues.summary: The corpus at 10,000 words is three times the bundle budget
issues.customerImpact: The delivery architecture cannot carry the stated plan
issues.evidence: `bundle:budget` forecasts 663.7 kB gzipped against a 220 kB budget from the measured 68 B/word. Not enforced; gated at 4,000 headwords.
issues.recommendedFix: Chunk the corpus by frequency band, split per locale, precache the shell and one locale and cache the rest on use.
issues.effort: MEDIUM — chunking and a cache policy

issues.summary: The traced guide is smaller than the demonstration for a single letter
issues.customerImpact: On a letter lesson the grey glyph a learner traces fills about half the writing square while the demonstration below it fills 0.84 of its own. Same letter, two sizes, one screen.
issues.evidence: Measured: Pretendard sets an isolated ㄱ at 0.53 × 0.42 of the box and eight per cent above its centre. Scaling the glyph to match was implemented and reverted: it scales the glyph's stroke too, from 0.057 of the box to 0.090 against a fixed 0.062 pen, and the robustness corpus went from 0.21% false rejections to 21% — one correct letter in five told it was wrong. See `features/writing/glyphSpec.ts`.
issues.recommendedFix: A grading model that does not measure coverage against a stroke the pen cannot fill, then the glyph can be sized for the eye. Its own calibration, not a side effect of a layout change.
issues.effort: MEDIUM–HIGH — a grading recalibration with its own corpus run

issues.summary: `strokes:measure:check` is not on the release gate
issues.customerImpact: None directly. The table is now reproducible and the check exists, but nothing runs it automatically, so a face upgrade could move the measurements without anyone being told.
issues.evidence: The original defect — `npm run strokes:measure` rewriting 23 of 33 syllables — was the script measuring a *fallback* face: the app ships Pretendard as a dynamic subset, and `document.fonts.load(font)` with no text loads only the Latin ranges, so `fillText` drew whatever the system had and the result depended on which subsets the app's own first screen had warmed. The script now loads the face for the text it measures, the table has been re-derived, and all 33 syllables were read by eye against the reference glyph. `npm run strokes:measure -- --check` passes repeatedly. What is left is that it is not in `verify:release`, because unlike every other gate it needs the app served on :4477.
issues.recommendedFix: Either have `measure-composition.mjs` start its own preview server when nothing is listening, or add the check to a release step that already has one, and then put it in `verify:release` beside `jamo:measure:check`.
issues.effort: LOW — one script change, or one gate entry

issues.summary: Longer explanations were English-only dictionary scrapings
issues.customerImpact: Non-English learners never saw the block; English learners read "phylum" under 문
issues.evidence: 25 written words in ten languages; §15.2.
issues.recommendedFix: done

issues.summary: Vietnamese and Thai vocabulary covered 500 of 2,581 words
issues.customerImpact: Past word 500 a vi/th learner read marked English
issues.evidence: 2,581 non-null rows in both.
issues.recommendedFix: done

issues.summary: Entries whose gloss contradicted their own example
issues.customerImpact: 열 read "fever" above a sentence about counting to ten
issues.evidence: Eleven found, all authored and pinned; `vocabulary:sense:qa:check` passes.
issues.recommendedFix: done

issues.summary: No matching exercise; production is tiles, not a keyboard
issues.customerImpact: Vocabulary still feels mostly like recognition on cards
issues.evidence: `build` was added; matching is still absent. Matching spans four words and the learning plan is per-word.
issues.recommendedFix: A session-level group exercise that can cover several word ids while crediting each word's evidence once. A scheduling change, not a screen.
issues.effort: MEDIUM — a session-level exercise concept, not a screen

issues.summary: Korean and English glosses describe different senses for some polysemous words
issues.customerImpact: The meaning changes when the interface language changes
issues.evidence: The eleven known cases are pinned. There is no automated guarantee a twelfth does not exist.
issues.recommendedFix: A canonical taught `senseId` per entry that every language's representation derives from.

issues.summary: Vocabulary listening questions relied on the hint ladder for a text alternative
issues.customerImpact: Usable, but scored as a reveal rather than as an accommodation
issues.evidence: There is no vocabulary listening question left to accommodate; §16.5. The letter exercises are I-21.
issues.recommendedFix: done

issues.summary: `sound_recognition` and `distinguish` letter exercises are heard-only, and the toggle that skipped them is gone
issues.customerImpact: A deaf learner arriving today meets letter questions they cannot answer. Anyone who had already turned the setting on keeps it — the stored `sound_free` flag is still honoured.
issues.evidence: No sound-free control in My Learning; `candidates()` still reads `sound_free` and still filters the letter modes.
issues.recommendedFix: A small per-question fallback on an audio-only letter question — "Can't use audio?" swapping in an equivalent visual recognition question, not revealing the answer and not penalised — rather than restoring a global setting.
issues.effort: LOW–MEDIUM — one per-question fallback, in 32 languages

issues.summary: A beginner's first sitting alternates two question layouts rather than four
issues.customerImpact: Ten new words, two shapes. The variety returns within days as words reach `review` and `familiar`.
issues.evidence: `stepsFor('new', i)` alternates `meaning` and `context`; two of the four checks were listening.
issues.recommendedFix: A non-listening third check for new words, if one can be recognition-only. The accepted cost of §16.5.
issues.effort: MEDIUM — a third non-listening check for new words

issues.summary: No export: clearing site data destroys the history irrecoverably
issues.customerImpact: A learner who clears browser data loses everything
issues.evidence: A consequence of having no account and device-local persistence. §24.6.
issues.recommendedFix: None that is customer-facing — a developer-style JSON export was tried and rejected. Keep IndexedDB robust, keep persistent storage requested, and do not warn normal users about it.

issues.summary: 243 of 2,581 words carry any verified lexical relation
issues.customerImpact: Synonym and antonym sections rarely appear
issues.evidence: `vocabulary:relations:qa`.
issues.recommendedFix: Nothing, unless a conservative source can be found. Sparse trustworthy data is not a defect and inventing similar words would be.
issues.effort: NONE unless a conservative source appears

issues.summary: 마디 was mispronounced in one voice
issues.customerImpact: One word sounded wrong
issues.evidence: Regenerated, fixtured, checked on-device.
issues.recommendedFix: done

issues.summary: The recogniser screen reported 낳다 as 낫다 in both voices
issues.customerImpact: None — the recordings are correct. The open question was the defect.
issues.evidence: The two readings differ measurably: 낳다 is [나타], an aspirated ㅌ with a short closure and a weak breathy release; 낫다 and 낮다 are both [낟따], a long closure and a sharp tense release. Measured off the shipped clips, both voices: 낫다 250/190 ms closure and −4.1/−2.9 dB release, 낮다 250/190 ms and −4.1/−2.8 dB, 낳다 170/170 ms and −6.9/−5.8 dB. The two [낟따] words are near-identical to each other and 낳다 is apart from both, in the direction aspiration predicts. `check_contrasts` in `qa_pronunciation.py` asserts this on every run, and fails if the pair is asserted the other way round.
issues.recommendedFix: done — the recogniser is not a normative judge of a clip and no longer gates this word.

issues.summary: No locale has been reviewed by a native speaker, across 32 interfaces
issues.customerImpact: Unknown awkwardness in thirty-one languages, and in Korean
issues.evidence: `docs/LOCALIZATION_NATIVE_REVIEW.md` states it. The severity was raised when the surface tripled.
issues.recommendedFix: Native review. Nothing automated substitutes for it, and no document here may claim it has happened.

issues.summary: 103 glosses carry more than one sense in some language
issues.customerImpact: 차 is "a car, or the tea you drink" on a beginner's card
issues.evidence: Reported by `vocabulary:sense:qa`; not gated.
issues.recommendedFix: One card, one taught sense. Additional senses belong in the Word Detail block, not in the quiz answer.

issues.summary: Word meanings exist in ten of the thirty-two interface languages
issues.customerImpact: Twenty-two languages read a fully translated app with English word cards
issues.evidence: Stated on the row in the language picker before the learner chooses, which is what makes it a limitation rather than a misrepresentation. §23.3.
issues.recommendedFix: Complete the shipping vocabulary content for the remaining twenty-two locales.

issues.summary: The *More about it* block is written for 25 words
issues.customerImpact: The other 2,556 word cards end at the example
issues.evidence: The alternative was 784 dictionary scrapings, which is why they were deleted.
issues.recommendedFix: Write it for the words that need it — polysemous, grammar-heavy, high-frequency functional, culturally specific, easily confused — starting with the top 500. Not a paragraph under every word.
